claims.statement: The Rust host is a hexagonal crate whose entry chain is main.rs -> galpi_lib::run() -> composition::run(), with domain/ (framework-free value objects and the worker-protocol parser), application/ (ports, the Application facade, JobRegistry, AppError), adapters/inbound/tauri.rs (all IPC commands and the event bridge), adapters/outbound/ (DesktopAdapter, NativeRecorder, LocalSettingsStore, process supervisor, setup/transcription/refinement/import modules), and composition.rs as the sole composition root.

The Rust dependency fence is executable: scripts/check-architecture.ts forbids crate::adapters, crate::composition, and tauri:: imports in domain/ and application/ (domain also cannot import crate::application), allows #[tauri::command] only in adapters/inbound/tauri.rs, allows generate_handler!/.manage(/.plugin( only in composition.rs, and confines tokio::process and nix:: signal primitives to adapters/outbound/process.rs and its process/ submodule; the fence runs as part of bun run check.

Application (application/use_cases.rs) is the single use-case facade: it holds the seven capability ports (EnginePort, TranscriptionPort, TranscriptImportPort, ArtifactPort, RecordingPort, SettingsPort, RefinementPort) as Arc<dyn ...> fields plus the JobRegistry and an active_recording tokio::Mutex<Option<Uuid>>; ports.rs declares nine traits in total (those seven capability ports plus the JobEvents and RecordingEvents event ports) alongside the RefinementJob parameter struct.

adapters/inbound/tauri.rs registers exactly seventeen #[tauri::command] functions that map 1:1 onto Application methods (diagnose_environment, prepare_environment, hugging_face_token_stored, save_hugging_face_token, load_assistant_settings, save_assistant_api_key, save_assistant_settings, save_engine_preset, refine_transcript, start_transcription, import_transcript, cancel_job, open_artifact, reveal_output_directory, start_recording, stop_recording, cancel_recording), and the commands are thin: deserialize camelCase input, call Application, return the mapped error.

Adding an IPC command is one change set spanning the #[tauri::command] in adapters/inbound/tauri.rs, registration in composition.rs's generate_handler!, a BackendPort method in src/domain/backend.ts, a Zod schema in src/adapters/tauri-backend.ts, and when applicable the docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section-2 table.

JobRegistry enforces a single active job: claim_with_id refuses with BUSY when the slot is held and with JOB_ID_CONFLICT when the requested id already has registered artifacts, and the returned JobGuard releases the slot on Drop so an early error, cancelled future, or panic cannot leave the registry permanently busy.

Cancellation through JobRegistry::cancel is synchronous oneshot delivery with distinct error codes: wrong id is JOB_NOT_FOUND, a second cancel is ALREADY_CANCELLING, and an already-finished job (receiver dropped) is JOB_FINISHED; JobRegistry's artifact map acts as the repository of finished work with ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND for unknown ids and STATE_ERROR for poisoned locks, and register_minutes attaches minutes to an existing entry.

Worker-process cancellation escalates in the supervisor, not the use case: process.rs selects on the cancel receiver while reading the child's pipes, sends SIGTERM to the whole process group, waits three seconds, then SIGKILLs and reaps, returning CANCELLED; the ProcessGroupGuard also SIGKILLs on Drop if still armed, so group teardown holds across panics and early returns.

Every IPC failure is AppError {code, message} with a stable ASCII machine-readable code and user-facing Korean message; AppError::io wraps raw io::Errors as IO_ERROR, adapters add codes such as WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR, PROCESS_FAILED, PATH_ERROR, SETTINGS_INVALID, and EVENT_ERROR, and the frontend's errorMessage() trusts only objects carrying both a string code and string message, falling back to generic Korean copy while errorDetail keeps the raw diagnostic.

Application enforces three use-case gates before adapter work: transcribe validates the speaker hint first (INVALID_SPEAKER_HINT, asserted to touch no workspace on rejection), transcribe refuses to run unless EnginePort::diagnose reports the saved preset ready (SETUP_REQUIRED), and refine_transcript reads the assistant API key only at refinement time, failing ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING when none is stored.

Value objects with business rules live in domain/ (roster.rs, job.rs, engine.rs, artifact.rs, worker.rs), while application/model.rs holds only serialization DTOs (EnvironmentStatus, result wrappers, recording types) mirroring the camelCase IPC wire; this placement is normative in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and was the subject of a recorded 2026-08 refactor.

AssistantSettings, Participant, and GlossaryEntry each carry a trimmed() rule: every string field is trimmed and blank becomes None, nameless participants are dropped entirely, blank aliases vanish, termless glossary rows vanish, and reasoning_effort is lowercased and kept only for low/medium/high/max; Application persists the trimmed form on save and reads through trimmed() on the refinement and ASR-context paths.

SpeakerHint is a mode-tagged domain enum (auto, exact count, min/max range) validated by validate_speaker_hint, which rejects zero counts and inverted ranges; the transcription adapter translates the variants into the worker's --num-speakers / --speaker-range flags.

EnginePreset is Qwen3 (the default) or the legacy WhisperX, serialized as "qwen3"/"whisperx" with unknown names rejected at deserialization; the saved preset selects which virtualenv interpreter, readiness markers, and ffmpeg binary the adapters use.

Artifacts is the aggregate for finished work (optional srt, checkpoint, minutes, source_audio plus required txt and output_directory); path_for(kind) is the only accessor, minutes_path derives <stem>_회의록.md by stripping the _화자별 suffix, and imported transcripts carry no srt/checkpoint/audio so opening those kinds fails with ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND.

domain/worker.rs owns both sides of the worker contract in the host: WorkerEvent is a snake_case-tagged six-variant enum (phase, completed, prepared, refined, error, log) flattened into a versioned {v, seq} envelope, parse_worker_event rejects malformed JSON and any protocol version other than 1, and AsrContext serializes glossary terms, participant names, and spoken aliases under the exact terms/names/aliases keys the worker's parse_asr_context reads, or stays absent when all three lists are empty.

Application::asr_context builds worker biasing context from the trimmed assistant settings (terms, then names, then aliases) and the adapters hand bulk or sensitive context to the worker through create_new 0600 temporary files deleted after the run -- --asr-context for transcription and background/participants/glossary files for refinement -- never through the argument vector.

DesktopAdapter deliberately implements five ports (EnginePort, TranscriptionPort, TranscriptImportPort, RefinementPort, ArtifactPort) in one type because Application is the sole consumer, with each port delegating to a sibling module under adapters/outbound/ (setup.rs, transcription.rs, import.rs, refinement.rs); the refinement interpreter stays on the WhisperX venv python while bulk context rides private temp files and the meeting date derives from source_audio's mtime.

Path containment is enforced in both directions: DesktopAdapter's ArtifactPort canonicalizes the artifact and the trusted output directory, requires the artifact to stay inside it and be a regular file before opening (ARTIFACT_PATH_ERROR/OPEN_ERROR), and every path a worker returns (artifacts, checkpoint, minutes) is canonicalized and must start with the job directory or the run fails WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR.

process.rs run_process is the host's only child supervisor, spawning with env_clear plus the explicit environment, null stdin, kill_on_drop, and its own Unix process group; stdout is read as bounded lines (64 KiB cap yields WORKER_PROTOCOL_ERROR) parsed by the domain protocol parser with a duplicate completed/refined event rejected, while stderr is batched into at most one log event per 100 ms or 32 lines with a 20-line tail so a non-zero exit reports PROCESS_FAILED with the last stderr line as detail.

Workers run under a fixed policy environment built by environment.rs: ko_KR.UTF-8 locale, PYTHONUTF8/PYTHONSAFEPATH/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, PYTHONPATH at the worker root, HF_HOME/TORCH_HOME/uv caches inside the app data directory, telemetry disabled, only uv-managed Pythons permitted, optional HF_TOKEN; assistant refinement extends it with GALPI_ASSISTANT_API_KEY/_BASE_URL/_REASONING_EFFORT, and Qwen3 transcription additionally sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 because it only runs after the readiness gate.

AppPaths resolves the app-local-data root into parallel WhisperX and Qwen3 engine layouts (each with its own venv python, readiness marker, models manifest, and bin directory with bundled ffmpeg), readiness for a preset means interpreter present plus a marker matching <version>+<requirements-hash> (so editing a requirements pin invalidates the venv) plus a valid models manifest and the expected Hugging Face cache directories, and prepare claims a job slot and installs only the missing pieces via bundled uv and the worker's prepare subcommand, failing SETUP_INCOMPLETE if the post-run status is still not ready; the default output root reported to the UI is ~/Documents/Galpi, and debug builds use repo binaries/ and worker/ paths while release builds use the bundle's uv and resources/worker.

LocalSettingsStore implements SettingsPort over one settings.json, holding a tokio::Mutex across each whole-document read-modify-write cycle with a cached parsed document (so concurrent saves cannot drop each other's fields, and a failed write invalidates the cache), deleting the file entirely when the settings are all-default, and returning assistant settings with api_key deliberately None and only api_key_stored set so the key value is read exclusively by load_assistant_api_key.

Both secrets (Hugging Face token, assistant API key) flow through the SecretStore trait; production currently wires SettingsFile (plaintext in settings.json) because macOS ties Keychain items to the creating code signature and the app ships ad-hoc signed, with the compiled Keychain implementation a one-line swap in LocalSettingsStore::new; secret reads are cached per launch (each keychain access can prompt the user), unchanged values are not rewritten, and legacy plaintext found in settings.json is migrated to the store and scrubbed from the file on first read.

NativeRecorder implements RecordingPort entirely through spawn_blocking, creates a meeting folder named after the recording so the .wav and later artifacts share one name, records to <name>.wav.part with the final .wav published only by atomic rename after finalize and duration validation, keeps the CPAL callback to sample conversion and bounded try_send (saturation is AUDIO_OVERRUN, channel loss WAV_WRITER_FAILED) while a writer thread owns Hound, periodic flushing, and the RIFF 4 GiB guard, and follows first-failure-wins: one RecordingFailure stored and emitted, later failures ignored, and the partial file removed on every failure path.

Recording is an independent single-slot resource outside the job registry: Application::start_recording mints a UUIDv7 and fails RECORDING_BUSY when a recording is active, stop/cancel verify the id (RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH for a foreign id, RECORDING_NOT_ACTIVE for an empty slot) and clear the slot regardless of the port call's outcome, so a user can record while a transcription runs but never record twice.

TauriEvents in the inbound adapter is the only bridge to the webview: one instance implements both JobEvents (emitting job-event with the WorkerEvent flattened under a camelCase jobId) and RecordingEvents (emitting recording-event with the RecordingFailure), emit failures map to EVENT_ERROR, and outbound adapters receive Arc<dyn JobEvents>/Arc<dyn RecordingEvents> so they stay Tauri-blind; the frontend consumes these via listenToJobs/listenToRecordingFailures in TauriBackend.

composition.rs is the only place concrete adapters are constructed and registered: it initializes the dialog and opener plugins, creates one TauriEvents shared as both event ports, clones DesktopAdapter into five port trait objects, wraps NativeRecorder and LocalSettingsStore behind their ports, app.manages the assembled Application, lists the seventeen handlers, and exits with status 1 on a failed run; Cargo lints deny unwrap/expect/panic across the crate, and the release profile keeps panic=unwind deliberately so a panic in the audio writer thread fails one recording instead of aborting the process.

New external capabilities follow a fixed extension path: trait in application/ports.rs, outbound implementation, composition.rs wiring, then FakePort extension in application/tests.rs; FakePort implements every port and is the only harness the application tests use, driving the real Application with no adapter internals mocked.

The application test suite pins end-to-end use-case behavior against FakePort: glossary/roster reach the worker as ASR context and nothing is sent when both are empty, cancellation reaches a running port producing CANCELLED without timing waits, refinement sends the saved key/model/background, filters attendees to the selection in roster order while always sending the global glossary, publishes minutes addressable as an artifact, imported transcripts refine without transcription, and the Hugging Face token is trimmed on save with whitespace meaning clear (prepare then uses the saved token when the request omits one).

The assistant API key has a dedicated write path: Application::save_assistant_api_key trims the input and clears the stored secret when it is blank, and the settings-autosave path LocalSettingsStore::save_assistant writes every roster/model/background field except the key, whose only entries are save_assistant_api_key and load_assistant_api_key — so an untouched stored key is never rewritten by a roster edit and an autosave can never erase it.
